title: Maria and the eclipse
hook: Maria bears him a son, Ibrahim, who dies as a baby, and on the day of an eclipse he says the sun and moon don't eclipse for anyone's death (Bukhari)
carry: the eyes weep, the heart grieves

segments.voice: Yesterday: Safiyyah and Maymunah, and a taunt that didn't go unanswered. Your line was he defended her.

The sky over Medina goes dim in broad daylight. The sun is being eaten from one side. Below, the town is in mourning; that same day a baby has died: Ibrahim, the son of the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him. People look up, and the talk begins. Of course the sun went dark. The heavens are grieving his son. It's a kind thing to say. It would comfort a father. Today: Maria, her son, and what he said under that dark sky.
screen: `THE SUN GOES DIM BY DAY.` → `A BABY HAS DIED THE SAME DAY.` → `THE HEAVENS ARE GRIEVING?`

segments.voice: Ibrahim's mother was Maria, remembered as Maria the Copt. Tradition, in Ibn Sa'd's biographies, says she came to Medina from Egypt, sent by its ruler. Some count her among the mothers of the believers; others give her a different standing, as the mother of his son. She's honored either way, and with her, our part on the mothers ends. In Sahih al-Bukhari, Anas tells of the day they went in to Ibrahim as he was dying. The Prophet's eyes filled with tears. Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf asked: you too, messenger of God? He answered: this is mercy. Then he said the line we carry today: the eyes weep, the heart grieves, and we say only what pleases our Lord. And to the child: we are saddened by your parting, Ibrahim. Tears, openly. Sorrow, named. And one limit: no words of protest against God. Then the eclipse. Another report in Bukhari, from al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah, says the sun was eclipsed on the day Ibrahim died, and people said it was for his death. The Prophet answered: the sun and the moon are two of the signs of God, and they are not eclipsed for anyone's death or life. When you see it, pray and call on God until it clears. He could have let the kind story stand; it was flattering, and about his own child. He corrected it on the day of his grief. That's why Muslims keep an eclipse prayer, salat al-kusuf: the dark sky becomes a time to pray, not a message about any one person. Real grief, and truth not bent to comfort it.
screen: `MARIA, MOTHER OF IBRAHIM.` · `THIS IS MERCY.` · `NOT FOR ANYONE'S DEATH OR LIFE.` · `THE ECLIPSE BECOMES A TIME TO PRAY.` · then, large: `THE EYES WEEP, THE HEART GRIEVES.`

segments.voice: Let one loss come to mind, and don't explain it or look for a sign in it; if tears come, let them, since the report calls them mercy. If you pray, say the Qur'an's line for a loss: "Lo! we are Allah's and lo! unto Him we are returning." If not, just say to yourself what is true: this hurt, and I miss them.
Kusuf, the eclipse, the dark sky the Prophet refused to call a sign for his son Ibrahim's death, even on the day he wept for him. Today's word.
Your line: the eyes weep, the heart grieves. Tears and truth can sit side by side. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: When a solar or lunar eclipse happens, Muslims gather for salat al-kusuf, the eclipse prayer, with long recitation and bowing; at a death, Muslims often say inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un, we belong to God and to Him we return.
